alt: Six finished wallpapers: three drawn in the smooth rendering along the top row, three in stranger rendering modes below.
caption: Wallpapers found by this project's fractal search. Nothing about them is hand-made: the search finds a good location on its own, a rendering mode draws it, a palette colors it, and a trained judge decides it is worth keeping. The top row is the classic smooth rendering; the bottom row is three of the stranger modes.
provenance: builder.picks — every panel is a seat of a recorded tentative gallery, named on this row by its own `<stamp>|<recipe key>` and resolved from artifacts/curation/tentative/<stamp>/gallery.jsonl for the seat and the candidate ledger for the recipe. Rendered fresh through the engine at 1280x720, supersample 3, then fitted to 422x237 in the sheet; the stored 640x360 thumbnail a seat points at is the picture the judges were shown and is not a source here. Nothing about the coloring is this figure's choice: mode, mode settings, curve, map, the whole palette pass and the cap all come off the ledger's recipe. Stamp 20260902T161757Z; panels in reading order, 3 across.

Autolevel: every candidate behind these seats was made with band_autolevel/v1 switched on, and a ledger recipe keeps only the reduced stamp of that — the operator, the switch and the band's sha256. The tone curve itself is a function of the render it was measured on, which a panel drawn at another size is not, so every panel here is the engine's own render of the recipe and no curve was replayed onto it. Held to that: each pick redrawn at the candidate's own 640x360 supersample 2 reproduces the stored picture its seat points at to mean absolute difference 2.9-4.9 of 255, codec floor 1.4-2.6, so the operator either did not act on any of the six or acted under what that record's own compression costs.

alt: Animated: three starting points advancing in step across the complex plane — one escaping fast, one bounded, one lingering near the boundary — with a |z|-versus-step chart alongside.
caption: Three orbits under the same rule, stepping together. One is past |z| = 2 within a few steps and gone for good, one stays bounded forever, and one hangs near the boundary for dozens of steps before it commits. The step where a track crosses the line on the chart is that orbit's escape time — the whole of what the picture is painted from.

alt: The Mandelbrot set with its real and imaginary axes marked and four colored rings on it, each ring's Julia set below in a frame of the same color — a solid blob from deep inside, filigree from the boundary, disconnected dust from outside.
caption: The Mandelbrot set read as an atlas of Julia sets. Each ring marks one value of c, and the Julia set that value draws is the panel below wearing the same color. A c from deep inside gives a solid, rounded blob; a c from outside shatters into dust; a c from the boundary unfurls its neighborhood's spirals and filaments across the whole frame. The blob-versus-dust split is not a matter of degree — a Julia set is connected exactly when its c lies in the Mandelbrot set.

alt: One Julia location under a cyclic ice palette at one, two, three and four sweeps of the gradient, each panel over a strip of the gradient repeated as many times as that panel spends it.
caption: One location and one cyclic palette, swept across the frame's range k times. At k = 1 the gradient is spent once over a range most of the frame does not occupy, and wide areas come out nearly flat; each further sweep spends it again and pulls more of the structure apart. Repetition is the classic escape from a squeezed range, and it is why so many older Mandelbrot renders are striped with rings.
provenance: scratch/render_fund/figures2.py cyclic_repeats() — four panels at 640x360, supersample 3, one location and one cyclic palette swept k times. The search produces admitted locations; mining draws and judges candidates at them, which accumulate into the pool; and curation chooses a gallery out of the pool as it stands. Each band's left half is the work and its right half is what the work produced, so an arrow runs out of one band's material and into the next band's process.
provenance: Drawn, not rendered: `python -m builder diagram wallpapers-stages`, from builder/diagrams.py. A PNG at 1316x506 on the stylesheet's own well, composed at the width every figure of this article is composed at. No engine render and no record read — the figure's subject is the shape of the three parts, which is the one thing on this page that no record holds. The wording of every box is this page's own prose reduced to two lines, and nothing on it is a count.

Three bands read top to bottom, each split at 46 per cent of the sheet's inner width into what a part does and what it produces. The material half is a step lighter than the process half, so the column a reader follows down the sheet reads as one column; the one band whose material is a store — the candidate pool — carries on that half alone the outline the two pools carry in pipeline-overview, because the band it sits in is a process like the other two.

Two elbow arrows, each out of a band's material and into the next band's process rather than straight down into the next band's own product: locations are what the pool was mined from, and an arrow drawn straight down would say they became it. No arrow runs back, which is the whole of what separates this figure from pipeline-overview on full-pipeline.html.
